newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, July 1.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, July 1.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index scored its biggest one-day gain in point terms for five years, in a pre-budget rally that caught analysts and dealers by surprise after weeks of cautious trading. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,728.3, up 123.7 points, or 2.69 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended bourse trade at a new closing high as the export-dependent chemical sector stole the spotlight, drawing strength from the dollar trading above 1.74 marks. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,819.85, up 34.08 points, or 0.90 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,834.84, up 67.95 points, or 1.80 percent.

PARIS - Shares extended their gains in afternoon trade, boosted by Wall Street's early advance on supportive U.S. data, to set a fresh closing high. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,944.04, up 85.78 points, or 3.00 percent.
ZURICH - Shares resumed their upward path following Monday's loss of more than one percent. The Swiss market index closed at 5,654.8, up 34.2 points, or 0.61 percent.

MILAN - Shares perked up in the last hour of trading, boosted by a strong opening on Wall Street and dollar strength, in line with major stock exchanges throughout Europe. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,477, up 295 points, or 2.24 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Shares closed firmer, with market players somewhat reassured by U.S. economic data released toward the end of the session. The AEX index closed at 871.31, up 9.76 points, or 1.13 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed with hefty losses as a mixture of trepidation ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and anxiety over the Nomura Securities Co Ltd scandal, which media reports say is widening, weighed on the market, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,175.52, down 429.44 points, or 2.08 percent.
HONG KONG - The stocks market continues to be closed as Hong Kong celebrates its return to Chinese rule. The market reopens on Thursday.

SYDNEY - Shares ended barely changed from Monday's record levels, as the strong underlying sentiment won over an early bout of profit-taking on the first day of the new financial year. The All Ordinaries index closed 4.7 points lower at 2721.2, down from a record close of 2725.9 on Monday. Turnover reached a healthy A$854.4 million.

JOHHANNESBURG - The easing of foreign exchange controls on South African individuals was welcomed by shares, lifting the industrial index to a new closing high despite a tumble in engineering firm Murray & Roberts. The All-share index closed at 7,420.1, up 0.1 points, or 0.00 percent. The All Gold index closed at 968.6, up 3.6 points, or 0.21 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,808.7, up 18.2 points, or 0.37 percent.
